local_facts.claim: North Carolina uses contributory negligence: an injured person’s negligence that joins with the other party’s negligence can bar recovery even if the contribution was comparatively small.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Fault statements and evidence must be handled carefully after a Concord crash; the collision report, scene evidence, witnesses and policy documents need to be checked before fault is conceded.
local_facts.title: A small fault allegation can have an outsized effect

local_facts.claim: Cabarrus County is in Superior Court District 25 and District Court District 25; the Cabarrus County Courthouse is at 61 Union Street South in Concord.
local_facts.why_it_matters: If a collision claim cannot be resolved, the proper court and local filing procedure matter. The early claim file should therefore preserve the report, evidence, records and insurance documents that may be needed later.
local_facts.title: Cabarrus civil cases have a local court structure

local_facts.claim: NCDOT’s I-85 Cabarrus project calls for an eight-lane divided facility over about 6.8 miles from south of Bruton Smith Boulevard/Concord Mills Boulevard to north of N.C. 73, with interchange modifications.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Crashes around Concord’s I-85 interchanges can involve multiple lanes, ramp movements and short-lived video evidence, so the exact location, direction of travel and scene records should be preserved quickly.
local_facts.title: The I-85 corridor has complex interchange evidence

pricing.table_head: What North Carolina law and the State Bar rule fix in a Cabarrus County injury claim
pricing.col_b: What the rule or statute sets

anchors.label: Percentage ceiling on an injury fee
anchors.detail: The State Bar rule bars a clearly excessive fee and lists eight factors for measuring one, but it names no percentage for a motor vehicle claim.

anchors.label: Superior court civil filing total
anchors.detail: The General Court of Justice fee of $180, a $16 facilities fee and a $4 telecommunications and data connectivity fee, paid when the complaint reaches the clerk.
anchors.source_name: N.C. Judicial Branch civil court costs chart

anchors.label: Ceiling on a medical provider lien
anchors.detail: A provider claiming against the recovery is limited by statute to half of the damages recovered, measured apart from attorneys' fees.

fee_rows.stage: Share of a car wreck recovery
fee_rows.note: North Carolina names no percentage. Reasonableness governs, measured by the difficulty, the result, local custom, and whether the fee is fixed or contingent.

fee_rows.stage: Form the agreement has to take
fee_rows.note: It must give the method, the percentages for settlement, trial and appeal, the expenses deducted, and whether they come off before or after.

fee_rows.stage: Fee tied to the result of a criminal charge
fee_rows.note: Barred outright for a criminal defendant, with a narrow carve-out for representation in a criminal or civil asset forfeiture proceeding.

fee_rows.stage: Workers' compensation fee on the same injury
fee_rows.note: The Industrial Commission weighs time invested, amount involved, results achieved, customary charge and skill, then allows what it finds reasonable.

fee_rows.stage: Opening a civil file with the clerk
fee_rows.note: Three totals, decided by the division the complaint goes to. Each already includes the facilities and connectivity add-ons.
fee_rows.source_name: N.C. Judicial Branch civil costs chart

fee_rows.note: Charged for every item the sheriff serves, so a wreck with two defendants and a corporate registered agent multiplies it.
